To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the consumption of a high-salt diet leads to a reduction of blood flow in the brain and to the formation of brain infarcts in mice.

1) salt intake is associated with increased blood pressure; 2) salt intake is a risk factor for cardiovascular events and stroke; 3) salt restriction reduces blood pressure in hypertensive and normotensive subjects; and 4) salt intake is related to cardiovascular mortality in the general population.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of sodium chloride (NaCl, table salt) and other sodium compounds (sodium bicarbonate, sodium citrate, sodium glutamate, sodium nitrate, sodium nitrite) in the etiology of cardiovascular disease.
how the social world is produced and reproduced through the use of language.
how people think about and use salt in food, and how they can be helped to make healthier food choices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is sufficient to conclude that sodium intake is a major determinant of hypertension and cardiovascular disease.
salt is a necessary part of a balanced diet, but in moderation.
the evidence is insufficient to conclude whether sodium chloride intake is a major factor in the etiology of hypertension or in the development of cardiovascular disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sodium chloride is a major contributor to cardiovascular disease and stroke, and the reduction of dietary salt intake is an essential component in the prevention and control of these diseases.
the consumption of salt, especially in the context of the Western diet, is a major contributor to the development of cardiovascular disease.
sodium intake is a significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can use the sodium intake of an individual as a predictor of cardiovascular disease risk and that the current recommended sodium intake of less than 2.3 g per day may be too low to prevent cardiovascular events, especially in older adults.
salt is an important factor in the development of heart disease, but it’s not the only factor.
we should all reduce our sodium intake.
